newsitem.title: UK: Barclays chief to head UK tax task force.
newsitem.headline: Barclays chief to head UK tax task force.

text.p: Martin Taylor, chief executive of Barclays Plc, will spearhead a government drive to modernise Britain's tax and benefit system, Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown announced on Monday.

Taylor will lead a Whitehall task force on tax and benefits to deliver the government's pledge to "streamline and modernise" the system to fulfil the objectives of promoting work incentives, a Treasury statement said.

The task force will bring together civil servants from the Treasury, the Inland Revenue and the departments of Social Security and Education and Employment. It will work closely with ministers in those departments.
Brown said Taylor would "bring to it a first rate mind and ability to find practical solutions to make a long-term difference."
Taylor will spend about two days a month on average on the project, which is expected to last for about a year.
"Today's appointment harnesses the drive of the private sector to the expertise of government departments to streamline both our tax and benefit systems," Brown said.

Social Security Secretary Harriet Harman said the task force would explore ways for the tax and benefits system to give people incentives to move into work. "We want to tear down the barriers that keep people out of jobs and trapped on benefit," she said. "Work is the best form of welfare for people of working age."
Brown is due to hold a budget within weeks. He has pledged to levy a windfall tax on Britain's privatised utilities, using the proceeds to get 250,000 people into work.
